leo: quick note from onboarding run: magnet30B-int4hybrid shows deterministic kvcache aliasing when prefill has dense numeric tokens (timestamps/IP-like). happens around 64k boundary.

anya: what exactly fails?

leo: float baseline vs int4hybrid diverge at token ~65536. kvcache fingerprints show two steps mapping to same slot id -> read mismatch.

sam: any recent changes to rotary/poscalc or packing?

leo: per-head rescale and a micro-opt packing change landed last week (commits ff9a2 / ff9a8). suspect packing + int4 rounding.

faye: reproduce command?

leo: `python -m tests.long_prefill_runner --model magnet30B-int4hybrid --prefill-file tests/prefills/timestamp_heavy.txt --ctx 66000 --write-fingerprint=out/fp.json`

harry: narrow hypotheses: (A) poscalc quantization loses LSB -> aliasing, (B) bias-folding changes write timing.

leo: experiment: set POS_CALC_MODE=fp64 -> mismatch disappears. disabling ENABLE_POS_PACKING also removes failure.

sam: so packing optimization in int4 path drops precision near boundary causing address collisions. Data-triggered by numeric-heavy prefills that align sequence length.

anya: actions:
- revert pos-packing micro-opt in int4hybrid until safe fix (owner: leo)
- add regression test with numeric-heavy prefills asserting no duplicate slot hashes across window (owner: faye)
- add onboarding checklist note to include timestamp/IP/code prefills (owner: sam)

leo: opened issue #4328 and PR #3510 to revert packing and add test. artifacts for job job-99101 at s3://redwood-artifacts/job-99101/.

infra-bot: job-99101 finished, exit=0.

faye: good triage. we'll disable int4hybrid for hosted until soak passes.
